newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends lower on USDA stocks data, soybeans.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends lower on USDA stocks data, soybeans.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed lower on USDA's May supply/demand and crop production reports and on a collapse in soybeans, traders said.

USDA Monday estimated 1996-97 U.S. corn carryover would total 909 million bushels. The figure proved bearish because some analysts had expected at least a slight decline in the carryover total. Analysts' estimates for corn carryover ahead of the report ranged from 869 million to 929 million bushels.
Also USDA Monday pegged 1997 U.S. corn production at 9.84 billion bushels which would be the second highest corn production on record in the U.S.
In 1994 the U.S. produced a record 10.103 billion bushels of corn.
Bearish input also came from USDA's weekly export inspections report.
USDA Monday said U.S. corn inspected for export during the week ended May 8 totaled 23.644 million bushels, near the low end of expectations for 23 million to 31 million bushels.
Corn futures closed 3-3/4 to five cents per bushel lower, with May down 3-3/4 at $2.88-1/4. July was down five cents at $2.83 and December closed 4-1/2 cents lower at $2.67-1/4.

ABN Amro-The Chicago Corp sold 3.5 million bushels of July, Iowa Grain sold three million July and Griffin Trading sold 1.5 million July, traders said. Prudential Securities bought 3.5 million July and Term Commodities bought two million bushels of December, traders said.
Corn futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 65,000 contracts, above the 44,190 traded Friday.

In corn options, Term Commodities bought 400 July $3.40 calls at 1/2 cent, Cargill Investor Services bought 200 December $3.60 calls at 2-1/8 to 2-3/8 cents and USA Trading bought 200 July $3.40 calls at 1/2 cent, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 17,000 contracts, slightly below the 17,227 traded Friday.
